motivation_audit.interpretation: Historical H1 remains valid for a globally broad but within-species sparse frame; it is not evidence that geographic barriers never organize flower colour.

questions.G1: Do adequately replicated independent species show excess recurrent broad geographic concentration of flower-colour discontinuity under an opportunity-conditioned species null?
questions.G2: Is the inferred recurrent field stable across species/photo Monte Carlo resampling and geographic/taxonomic deletion?
questions.G3: What are the prevalence, central tendency and between-species heterogeneity of species-specific spatial colour organization?
questions.G4: Only if G1 passes, do independently frozen barrier surfaces align with the recurrent field?

metadata_only_feasibility.automatic_rule: select the largest raw-photo target that yields at least 300 metadata-eligible species; if none does, stop before pixels
metadata_only_feasibility.photo_selection: deterministic geographic maximin with deterministic hash tie-break

measurement.path: qualified ROI-v4 flower mask plus fixed generic CIELAB palette

outer_monte_carlo.photo_sampling: seeded balanced random blocks within species

species_geometry.G3_species_statistic: Spearman pairwise great-circle distance versus pairwise colour JSD across 20 photos

global_field.species_weight: equal total contribution within each resample
global_field.primary_statistic: opportunity-weighted spatial concentration of the consensus field

null.shuffle: classifiable colour vectors within species only

stability_outputs: within-species Monte Carlo spread of G3 rho and field contribution
leave-one-major-family-out for families >=5% of inferential species
claim_ceiling: G1 support establishes recurrent broad geographic concentration of flower-colour discontinuity across globally sampled adequately replicated species under this frozen opportunity-conditioned design; it does not establish a universal exact boundary or a causal climate, topographic, pollinator or pigment mechanism.
